newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude firms but paper spreads, CFDs ease.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude firms but paper spreads, CFDs ease.

text.p: North Sea crude strengthened early on Wednesday on mildly bullish U.S. weekly inventory data but Brent spreads and contracts for difference eased, traders said.

June Brent was trading 15 cents up at $18.14 a barrel by 1202 GMT, compared with its 35-cent slip on Tuesday when it settled at $17.99 on the back of a sharp sell-off on NYMEX ahead of the expiry of its WTI May contract.
Oil futures rallied on Wednesday on the back of what traders said were slightly bullish American Petroleum Institute (API) weekly U.S. inventory data, issued on Tuesday night.
The API showed a 4.7 million barrel draw on middle distillates, defying market expectations of a half-million barrel decline. It also showed a gasoline draw of 1.9 million.
There were no reported trades on the physical market by noon Wednesday but traders said a European equity holder sold two Forties cargoes loading May 22-24 and 24-26 on a p+c basis on Tuesday.

Forties was talked a couple of cents firmer at Dated Brent +10/+14 cents and other North Sea grades also showed signs of moving higher, Ekofisk valued around Date Brent +15 cents from +12 cents on Tuesday.
One Brent cargo clocked to Esso on Tuesday was deferred and due to pass through the paper chains on Wednesday, traders said. Cargill was five o'clocked with the second Brent on Tuesday.
Brent intermonth spreads weakened slightly with May/June talked at -22/-18 cents from -19/-15 cents.
Likewise, Brent CFDs eased with next week shedding some nine cents to June Brent -44/-38 cents while May 2-9 was talked June Brent -38/-33 cents.
Traders said Dubai crude eased slightly in a quiet market with June Dubai last talked at Brent +$1.50/$1.60 and July Dubai at Brent +$1.45/$1.55 in early talk.
